rv.q: Michael Griffo's warm, evocative language and the excellent acting in this two-hander make Pen Pals, currently playing at Theatre at St. Clement's, truly special.
Pen Pals sneaks up on you; by the finale, these women feel like old friends.
Vardalos, especially, made us believe that we’re getting to know a full human being who just happens to express herself through two-dimensional text.

Judging from the laughs or recognition and the sniffling of sadness for some revelations, Griffo’s play seems to hit a nerve with the mostly older audience, especially the emotionally charged ending that leaves the audience on a high.
Pen Pals is a cozy night out, a sharing of distaff confidences that may well follow a production trajectory not unlike that of Love Letters.
What is not discussed is the volatile world these two lived in.

cn.t: Critics praise Michael Griffo's warm epistolary drama for its evocative writing and excellent performances, finding it a compelling exploration of friendship that successfully mines genuine emotion from its characters' everyday joys and sorrows.
